cohort: 46 pairs of monochorionic twins with selective fetal growth restriction (FGR), aged 3 to 17 years at follow-up.
finding: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) itself, rather than early postnatal catch-up growth (CUG), was found to have negative consequences for cognitive development.
followup_time: Median 11 years (IQR 8-13 years) for cognitive outcome, with catch-up growth measured at 2 years.
birth_weight: Varied, assessed by birth weight z-score.
gest_age: Varied, assessed by gestational age at birth.
